title: observability logs metrics tracing alerts and OpenTelemetry
concepts: Observability uses emitted telemetry to infer internal behavior from outside the system. Logs, metrics, and traces answer different questions; correlation IDs and context propagation connect them without making any one signal a substitute for the others.

Instrumentation must preserve useful context while controlling cost, cardinality, sensitive data, and sampling loss. Semantic conventions provide shared attribute names, but stability status and schema migration still matter.

A service-level indicator measures an outcome users care about; an SLO states a target over a window, an error budget makes tolerated unreliability explicit, and alerts should identify actionable symptoms rather than every noisy cause.

OpenTelemetry separates APIs and SDKs from the OTLP protocol and Collector pipeline. Receivers, processors, exporters, connectors, extensions, and service pipelines are configured and enabled independently; component availability and stability differ by distribution.

Metrics summarize measurements across dimensions, logs preserve event details, and traces connect spans across a request path. Sampling, histogram design, exemplars, resource identity, and high-cardinality labels change what questions can be answered and at what cost.

Operational evidence should support a repeatable investigation: detect impact, establish scope and timeline, inspect correlated signals, verify recovery, and capture follow-up actions. Dashboards without ownership, thresholds, or response procedures do not constitute monitoring.

items: Current semantic-convention documentation publishes version 1.45.0. Individual conventions have their own stability status; instrumentation may expose opt-in migrations such as OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN rather than changing emitted names without a compatibility plan.

Prometheus 3.0 introduced UTF-8 metric and label name support while recommending conventional names for cross-tool compatibility. Current documentation includes native histograms and corresponding scrape configuration; distinguish native histograms from classic bucket series.

scopeExclusions: Vendor backend dashboards, query languages, and pricing are not universal; provider-specific operations belongs to t09-007
Application-specific .NET ILogger, OpenTelemetry SDK configuration, and auto-instrumentation APIs are covered in language/runtime tracks
Incident command and response procedures are operational practice; t09-009 covers execution while this inventory defines core telemetry and alert vocabulary
Security audit strategy and privacy regulation are in t07; telemetry redaction is included only as an instrumentation safeguard
Profiling is included as a related signal but exact vendor profiler APIs are excluded

The OpenTelemetry Collector registry contains hundreds of optional components; this source-bounded map names the core architecture and commonly used components, not every third-party distribution plugin
